THIS MFA IS FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED- 03.02.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.172/2010 ON THE FILE OF MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AT JEWARGI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the MACT at Jewargi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.172/2010 and the liability fastened on the owner to pay the compensation vide judgment and award dated 03.02.2012.
2.
The appellant/claimant had suffered injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 06.02.2009 involving a Tata Ace vehicle bearing registration No.KA-32/A-3714.
The claimant suffered fracture of distal shaft of left tibia, degloving injury and loss of skin and bones and also cut lacerated wound on the posterior aspect of left ankle and other injuries.
She was shifted to Basaveshwar Hospital, Kalaburagi where she was treated as an inpatient for 3 months.
Implants were used to treat the fracture and skin grafting was done several times.
She claimed that she had to undergo operation for removal of implants.

She claimed that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the aforesaid vehicle and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.14,30,000/-.
3. The claim petition was contested by the insurer who denied the accident as well as its liability to pay the compensation.

It specifically contended that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a licence to drive Light Motor Vehicle non-transport while the vehicle in question was a transport vehicle used for carrying goods.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P17.
She also examined a doctor as PW.2.

The insurer on the other hand examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 and R2.
4.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal considered her notional income at Rs.1,500/- per month and the disability suffered by her at 15%.

The Tribunal determined the compensation as follows:
1 Pain and suffering Rs.15,000/- 2 Loss of amenities and impairing of Rs.20,000/-
future life 3. Medical expenses Rs.9,000/-

4. Attendant charges and extra Rs.4,000/-
 nourishment and conveyance  charges 5.

Towards loss of studies and school Rs.10,000/- days 6. Towards loss marriage prospects Rs.15,000/-
7. Towards loss of future income Rs.40,500/-
Total Rs.1,13,500/-

5. However, insofar as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed only a licence to drive non-transport vehicle and did not possess an endorsement to drive a transport vehicle.
Therefore, it held that the owner of the offending vehicle alone was liable to pay the entire compensation as determined by the Tribunal.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded as well as the liability fixed on the owner of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation, the claimant is in appeal before this Court.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the claimant was a 10 year old girl and the disability was determined at 15% by the Tribunal as against the evidence of PW.2 who deposed that the disability suffered by the claimant was 28%.

He submitted that even as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- in addition to the actual expenditure (2014) 14 SCC 396 incurred for treatment, attendant charges etc.

ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED2, the insurer cannot escape from the liability on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess an endorsement to drive a transport vehicle.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the contention urged by the insurer is fully covered by the judgment of the Apex Court referred above.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent - Insurer submitted that the claimant was 10 years old and the fractures are united as per the evidence of PW.2 and therefore, the compensation determined by the Tribunal is just and proper.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent - Insurance Company.
I have also perused the records of the Tribunal and its judgment.
9. When the accident in question occurred on 06.02.2009, the claimant was 10 years old.
The evidence of PW.2 clearly discloses that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 28% to Laxmi D/O Ramanna @ Ambanna Madiwal vs Shankar Rathod S/Oharishchandra ...

on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56522335/
3

the limb and having regard to the nature of injuries sustained and also having regard to the fact that the insurer has not challenged the finding regarding disability, this Court is of the view that the disability assessed by the Tribunal at 15% to the whole body of the claimant deserves to be maintained.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in MASTER MALLIKARJUN (supra), the claimant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- in addition to the compensation towards re-imbursement of medical expenses, attendant charges etc.

The judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN (supra) dealt with an accident that occurred on 05.06.2006 and therefore, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled towards pain and suffering deserves to be enhanced marginally by taking inflation.

10. In that view of the matter, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,63,000/-
towards pain and suffering.

In addition, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/-
towards discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization.
She is also entitled to medical expenses of Rs.9,828/- and incidental expenses of Rs.15,000/- apart from future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-.

11. In view of the above, the claimant is entitled to total compensation as follows:
1. Pain and suffering Rs.3,63,000/-
2. Discomfort, inconvenience and Rs.40,000/-
loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization 3.

Medical expenses Rs.9,828/-
4. Incidental charges Rs.15,000/-
5. Future medical expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Rs.4,57,828/-
12.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN (supra), the insurer cannot escape the liability to pay the compensation as the driver of the offending vehicle was otherwise eligible to drive a Light Motor Vehicle (transport) and therefore, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
13. In that view of the matter, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.4,57,828/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.3,44,328/- shall be paid by the insurer - 10 - Laxmi D/O Ramanna @ Ambanna Madiwal vs Shankar Rathod S/Oharishchandra ... on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56522335/
4 along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text:
The insurer is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the compensation and interest as determined by this Court shall be deposited in the name of the appellant/claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period 3 years.
In view of disposal of main appeal, I.A.1/2022 for production of additional documents stands disposed of.
